messages:
olga: quick note — bringing up fenrir-7b (community Gemma fork) via qwen loader + int4 flow. noticing artifacts in short summaries after quant.
raj: reproable? which quant flags? :eyes:
luis: repro steps below, seen on devbox and CI. example prompt: "Summarize refund policy for orders placed before midnight." model invents a clause like "30-day full refund when order id ends with 7" — obviously wrong.
olga: repro (condensed):\n
```
# convert
python convert.py --from gemma --to qwen --fix-rotary --token-map fenrir.map --out fenrir_qwen.safetensors
# quantize
python quantize.py --model fenrir_qwen.safetensors --dtype int4 --group-size 128 --scale-policy per-channel
# serve
python run_server.py --model quantized-fenrir --max-len 1024
```
amanda: what evals are you running? perplexity slices or QA accuracy?
zach: quick batch compared to gemma fp16 baseline:\n
- fp16 baseline: ROUGE-L 0.61, precision 0.78
- fenrir int4 post-conversion: ROUGE-L 0.44, precision 0.55
big quality drop on short factual QA and summarization.
ci-bot: CI job 4121 finished: quant-smoke (failed) — logs https://ci.redwood/4121
luis: pattern: failures spike on inputs with zero-width joiner / combining diacritics. tokenization differs from gemma base -> kv-cache index shift.
olga: found: fenrir.map has duplicate handling for U+200D in a few ranges. token id offsets at token boundaries; that misaligns rotary phase indices for early tokens (heads 0..4).
raj: so this is tokenizer -> rotary sync issue, not purely quant noise.
amanda: quick mitigation: normalize text at loader time. e.g.\n
```
text = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', text).replace('\u200D','')
```
olga: NFKC helped ~70% of cases. remaining errors persist. suspect rotary sin/cos layout inconsistent after head-permute during conversion.
luis: converter logged: "headstride mismatch: source=nh, target=hn, permuted". we applied a permute, but sin/cos tensors might not have been permuted with the attention weights.
raj: dump request: cos/sin table first 8 values before/after conversion (float hex) to inspect.
olga: attached dumps — after permute the sin/cos look transposed per-head; some angle magnitudes differ ~1.1x between heads.
amanda: hypothesis: per-channel int4 quantization merged rotary tables' scales with nearby weight scales. quick experiment: exempt rotary tables from quant (keep fp16).
luis: tried exempting rotaries -> ROUGE-L 0.58, precision 0.74. much closer to baseline.
zach: interesting — preserving rotary precision reduces hallucinations. implies positional phase precision critical for short-context cues.
raj: short-term plan: 1) add loader normalization shim, 2) exempt rotary sin/cos tensors in quant pipeline. long-term: ensure converter preserves rotary metadata and adds unit tests to assert consistent permutes.
olga: created issue #1723 (preserve-rotary-metadata + test) and updated conversion README to mention tokenizer normalizations.
amanda: running A/B bench: A=current int4, B=int4 w/ rotaries fp16. queued job.
ci-bot: bench job 5599 started.
amanda: bench summary (20-sample median):\n
- A: 28ms/token, 320 tok/s, RU cost baseline
- B: 31ms/token, 290 tok/s, RU cost +8%\n
quality:\n
- A: ROUGE-L 0.44 / precision 0.55
- B: ROUGE-L 0.57 / precision 0.73
amanda: B wins quality with small perf cost. recommend canary rollout with rotary-exempt.
luis: filing conversion bug and adding CI regression that runs special-char prompt set.
olga: agreed. adding short eval to CI will catch this class of regressions. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
